title: Hi-hat rolls and movement
summary: The four roll rates, velocity ramps and pitched rolls, and where rolls go so they push the beat forward instead of cluttering it.

steps.title: Faster than the grid
steps.body:
A **roll** is a burst of hats faster than the grid's 16th steps. In the drum grid, switch to **Roll**, pick a **Rate** and drag along the **HAT** row.

- **1/32**: two hits per step. A quick stutter.
- **1/16T**: three hits across two steps. A triplet gallop that pulls against the straight grid.
- **1/32T**: three hits per step. A buzz.
- **1/64**: four hits per step. Almost one smear of sound.

Rolls work like fills: a burst of tension that lands on the next big hit. That's why they cluster **right before the snare** and at the **end of a bar**.

Next: straight hats vs rolled.
steps.deeper:
**The math.** The app counts 96 ticks per beat, so one 16th step is 24 ticks. A 1/32 roll puts hits 12 ticks apart (two per step), 1/32T 8 apart (three per step), 1/64 6 apart (four per step). 1/16T puts them 16 apart, three across two steps, so drag it across an even number of steps to land back on the grid.

At 140 BPM a beat lasts about 0.43 seconds. A 1/64 roll packs 16 hits into it, about 37 a second, so fast it reads more like a buzz than separate hits.

**Triplets** split time into threes where the rest of the beat splits into twos and fours. A 1/16T roll briefly rubs against the straight grid, and that rub is the gallop.

**Why before the snare or at the end of a bar?** A roll raises the energy, and the ear wants it to land somewhere. The snare, or beat 1 of the next bar, is the landing.

steps.title: Straight vs rolled
steps.caption: 140 BPM half-time, same kick and snare in all three. Only the hats change.

examples.label: Straight 8ths
examples.explanation: Steady and tidy. It keeps time, but nothing pushes forward.

examples.label: 8ths with two rolls
examples.explanation: A 1/16T roll into the snare in bar 1, and a 1/32 run over the last beat of bar 2 into the loop restart. Same hats otherwise, and the beat leans forward.

examples.label: Rolls everywhere
examples.explanation: A roll in every beat. It's busy the whole way through, so no single roll leads anywhere.

steps.title: Shape the roll
steps.body:
Rate is only the start. Three more things shape a roll:

- **Ramp.** In Roll mode, **Ramp** sets loudness from first hit to last. **Up** swells into the next hit, **Down** fades out of one, **Flat** keeps every hit the same.
- **Pitch.** Trap producers often pitch a roll up or down as it runs. This grid plays every hat at one pitch, so pitched rolls are one for Koala.
- **Placement.** The steps just before the snare push into it. The end of bar 2 sets up the loop restart. Put rolls everywhere and they stop meaning anything.

For single hits, hold a hit in **Draw** mode to set its velocity.

Next: flat vs ramped.
steps.deeper:
**Ramps in the grid.** Up runs from about a third of full loudness to full. Down runs the other way. Flat sits at three quarters. An Up ramp into the snare is the classic swell. A Down ramp right after a hit sounds like it's dying away.

**Pitched rolls** step the hat up or down in pitch as the roll runs, often rising into a big moment or falling out of one. The movement in pitch adds a direction on top of the speed. In Koala, try it by playing a hat sample at different pitches.

**Ghost hats.** Quiet hits between the main ones add movement without adding volume. In Draw mode, hold a hat, then drag the velocity slider that appears to the left. A pattern of loud and quiet hats grooves even with no roll at all.

steps.title: Flat vs ramped
steps.caption: Clips can only change loudness step by step, so these ramps run over a 16th-note run at the end of bar 2. The **Ramp** setting does the same thing inside a roll.

examples.label: Flat
examples.explanation: Eight 16th hats at the end of bar 2, all the same loudness. It speeds up, but it doesn't build.

examples.label: Ramp up
examples.explanation: The same eight hats, quiet to full. They swell into beat 1 as the loop comes round.

examples.label: Ramp down
examples.explanation: Full to quiet. The run fades out before the loop restarts: calmer, less push into beat 1.

steps.title: Roll it
steps.prompt:
Add rolls to this beat (or to your own, if Your Track has drums):

1. Switch the mode to **Roll**, then pick a **Rate** and a **Ramp**.
2. Drag along the **HAT** row across a step or two: try steps 7–8 in **Bar 1**, right before the snare, or steps 13–16 in **Bar 2**.
3. Play it, then try another rate. In Roll mode, tap a roll to clear it.

Keep at least **8 hats** across both bars, so the clock keeps ticking around your rolls.
hints: Rolls only happen in **Roll** mode, and only with a drag: a tap won't make one. Switch the mode, then drag sideways along the **HAT** row.
On a narrow screen, Roll mode shows half a bar at a time: switch with **Steps 1–8** and **Steps 9–16**. For **1/16T**, drag across two steps so the roll ends back on the grid.
Try this: **Bar 1**, Rate **1/16T**, Ramp **Up**, drag the **HAT** row across steps 7–8 into the snare. Then **Bar 2**, Rate **1/32**, drag across steps 13–16.
